•single point mut in factor V gene → insensitive to activated protein C (natural anticoagulant)
Coag pathways: extrinsic (factor III + VII) + intrinsic (XII, XI, IX, VIII) → activate X → common (X, V, II, I, XIII) → stable clot
↑incidence of DVT, PE, hepatic v., or cerebral v. thrombosis

•DNA analysis: reliable in preg, acute thrombosis + w/ anticoagulation
Proteins C & S are vit K-dependent anticoag proteins produced by the liver that stim fibrinolysis & inactivate factors V & VIII
: ESLD, severe liver dz w/ synthetic dysfun, early warfarin admin.
•⇡VTE risk w/ prolonged immobilization, surg, smoking, preg, OCPs/exogenous estrogen
•MCC of ⇣protein C other than deficiency: VKA (warfarin) tx + liver dz
•esp leg DVT, PE, mesenteric v. thrombosis; adverse preg outcomes (fetal loss, miscarriage)
•transient hypercoagulable state from protein C depletion when starting warfarin
: red purpuric lesions @ P points, progresses to painful black eschars
protein C & S funct assay, plasma protein C & S Ag levels

•protein S functional assay <55%: ⍉reliable in preg, acute thrombosis, or w/ anticoagulation
- DOACs more common for typical VTE; warfarin may be preferred for unusual/severe presentation or large clot
- duration: provoked vs unprovoked; unprovoked VTE + thrombophilia → may be indefinite
